edits.new: Changing independent array comparisons to $elemMatch changes query meaning as well as enabling bound intersection. Without $elemMatch, the same element need not satisfy both conditions and MongoDB cannot intersect the bounds; with $elemMatch, the array must contain at least one single element matching all conditions. Treat this as a semantic decision before optimizing an array filter that precedes sorting. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md

edits.old: Ascending array sorts use the lowest array element; descending sorts use the highest. A predicate restricting matching array elements does not redefine the document's sort key. SERVER-31898 illustrates why scanning only myArray >= 5 would misorder arrays [1,6,7] and [3,4,5]. (high confidence)

evidence.quote: The new behavior is to sort documents according to the lowest-valued element of the array for ascending sorts, and according to the highest-valued element of the array for descending sorts.

If we were to use an index scan with bounds [5, Infinity] to answer this query, then these documents would sort incorrectly---the second document would use 5 as its sort key and the first document would use 6.
Prior to this change, the find command's behavior was similar to the above, except the smallest in-bounds element was selected as the sort key.

edits.old: A multikey index creates separate entries for distinct array values, so one document can have multiple index entries. For array sorting, MongoDB generates the set of keys for the sort pattern and uses the minimum key by index ordering as the document-level sort key; an individual entry is therefore not generally the document's sort key. (medium confidence)

(medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-19402

evidence.quote: For each distinct value in the array, MongoDB creates a separate entry in the index, and each entry points back to the same document.

To determine the sort key for a document d given sort pattern p, we generate the set of index keys K for d by treating p as an index key pattern. The sort key is min(K), where min is determined by the index ordering.

statements.statement: A multikey index creates separate entries for distinct array values, so one document can have multiple index entries.
For array sorting, MongoDB generates the set of keys for the sort pattern and uses the minimum key by index ordering as the document's sort key.

edits.rationale: The multikey docs state one document can have multiple entries. SERVER-19402 states the sort key is min(K) of the keys generated from the sort pattern, by index ordering, so a single entry is not generally the sort key.

edits.rationale: The multikey bounds page documents that $elemMatch makes MongoDB intersect bounds. The sort-with-indexes page states that sorting on a multikey-indexed array field needs an in-memory sort unless the bounds for all sort fields are [MinKey, MaxKey] and no multikey field's bounds share the sort pattern's path prefix. The claim joins these two documented rules and says it is an inference. The sources support it, and narrowed bounds on a sort field would actually work against the full-bounds condition.
